In [30]:
# Create empty columns
monthly["IQR_Lower"] = np.nan
monthly["IQR_Upper"] = np.nan
monthly["IQR_Anomaly"] = False

# Calculate IQR separately for each product category
for category in monthly["CategoryName"].unique():

    mask = monthly["CategoryName"] == category

    Q1 = monthly.loc[mask, "Quantity"].quantile(0.25)
    Q3 = monthly.loc[mask, "Quantity"].quantile(0.75)

    IQR = Q3 - Q1

    lower_bound = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR
    upper_bound = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR

    monthly.loc[mask, "IQR_Lower"] = lower_bound
    monthly.loc[mask, "IQR_Upper"] = upper_bound

    monthly.loc[mask, "IQR_Anomaly"] = (
        (monthly.loc[mask, "Quantity"] < lower_bound) |
        (monthly.loc[mask, "Quantity"] > upper_bound)
    )

IQR vs Z-Score Analysis¶

The IQR method detected 30 anomalies, while the Z-Score method detected 7 anomalies.

7 anomalies were identified by both methods.

The difference occurs because Z-Score measures observations using the mean and standard deviation, whereas IQR identifies values outside the lower and upper quartile-based boundaries.

These detected observations represent unusual demand patterns that require further business investigation before determining their actual cause.

for category in monthly["CategoryName"].unique():                         ## Apply Isolation Forest Category-Wise

    mask = monthly["CategoryName"] == category

    category_data = monthly.loc[mask, ["Quantity"]].dropna()

    model = IsolationForest(
        contamination=0.05,
        random_state=42)

    predictions = model.fit_predict(
        category_data[["Quantity"]])

    monthly.loc[category_data.index,"IF_Anomaly"] = predictions == -1

Comparison of Anomaly Detection Methods¶

Three anomaly detection methods were evaluated: Z-Score, IQR, and Isolation Forest.

Z-Score identifies extreme observations based on the mean and standard deviation, while IQR detects values outside quartile-based boundaries. Isolation Forest uses a machine-learning approach to identify observations that are easier to isolate from normal demand.

The results from all three methods were compared category-wise. Observations detected by at least two methods were prioritized as higher-confidence anomaly candidates. This combined approach can help reduce unnecessary alerts while highlighting unusual demand patterns that require business investigation.

Z-Score detected: 7 anomalies

IQR detected: 30 anomalies

Isolation Forest detected: 15 anomalies

Detected by at least two methods: 5 anomalies

Detected by all three methods: 7 anomalies
